items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: Anyway, he would come to our house and he would play, and I just couldn't believe a piano could sound that beautiful.

ctx.x: I ever heard. James Morgan was sort of known as a child prodigy. At that time, I was I guess about 14 years old, and James Morgan was about 18 then. Anyway, he would come to our house and he would play, and I just couldn't believe a piano could sound that beautiful. He'd play some of the popular things, like... I remember, he was the first one that I think I heard play "Sophisticated Lady," and there was a tune out there, popular then, called "Out In The Cold Again." The one that I was really impressed with was a…

But this fellow used to play all of these things. His name was James Morgan. He just died. I think James Morgan died around 1978. He was the kind of guy that never left Washington -- for what reasons, I don't know, because everybody would try to get him to leave. Other bandleaders would come here, and try to coax him away from Washington. But as far as I know, James Morgan never went across the bridge to Alexandria, Virginia.
